newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.12 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.12 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.12 percent to close at 1.0642 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market following the Central Bank's lowering of the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank depreciated the mini-band by 0.14 percent to between 1.0615 and 1.0665 reais per dollar.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.43 percent against the dollar compared with an average drop of between 0.5 and 0.6 percent over the past four months.
The real's fall was also due to continued arbitrage plays by some banks that bought dollars in the spot commercial market and sold May forex future contracts, dealers added.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.08 percent to end at 1.0665 per greenback.
In the parallel market, the real closed flat at 1.135 per dollar, traders said.
